title: Hi-Lo: card tags
subtitle: Update the count from cards, without independent-task hints.

theory.text: Hi-Lo tags are not blackjack points: 2–6 add +1; 7–9 add 0; 10, J, Q, K and A add −1. Start running count (RC) at zero after a shuffle and add each exposed card’s tag once. For example, 5 raises RC by one and K lowers it by one. A tag does not depend on its seat or whether the hand wins. Introductory cards show tags; practice hides them unless you ask for a hint, and independent tasks have no hints. Enter the sum of all tags, including the final two-card example. This is a closed training simulation, not an external table counter.

coaching.explanation: 5: (+1) = +1. Starting RC 0 plus this change gives +1. Neutral cards do not contribute; count each revealed card once.
coaching.contrast: Compare 2, K (0) with 2, 3 (+2): grouping saves effort, but the signs of the tags still matter.

title: Hi-Lo: count a chunk
subtitle: Update the count from cards, without independent-task hints.

theory.text: Read a chunk as one change in running count: add the tags of its 3–5 cards, then add that change to the starting count. For example, 2, 4, Q sum to +1; 2, 4, Q, A sum to 0. Neutral 7–9 do not change the sum. A chunk need not cancel to zero. Each group below appears at once so that you practise the group rather than use per-card feedback. On independent tasks no tags, cancellation markers or correct RC are shown. The cards and your first answer survive leaving the lesson.
